question: Would one evidence-focused review opportunity repair Qwen v5 citation and stopping failures better than a generic second look, before we consider more training?

task.value: Known-paper QASPER Python-tool agent; historical development analysis

model.value: Qwen3-8B with Qwen Envoy v5 adapter

hardware.value: Historical serving: NVIDIA A40 48GB; future trial hardware not selected

workload.value: Five already-seen illustrative cases; no untouched test claim

constraints: Planning only: zero model requests, GPU launches, or paid calls in Task 5. The positive trial ceilings below are a proposal requiring separate approval.
No training or model-weight changes. Do not send gold answers, case labels, existing grades, or paper grader notes to either trial arm.
Keep model-authored Python execution in Docker. Preserve the V1 tool preamble and use the same tools and shared initial state in both arms.

observations.text: Both September 30 models have 3/20 provisional answerable passes; the 5/40 to 15/40 aggregate includes refusal behavior.
The dataset trace reads text containing the dataset name but submits an earlier unrelated span; fixing retrieval alone may not repair citation selection. This interpretation is model-assisted.
The SEPT trace stops after abstract-level retrieval and misses the requested simplifications. This suggests an exploration/stopping diagnostic but does not identify a cause.
A fixed-BM25 one-shot comparator was already run, with official token-overlap F1 41.52/58.86 for base/v5. Support remains unreviewed; do not rerun it as a novel proposal.

Self-RAG trains reflection; ALCE separates citation support; intrinsic self-correction can hurt in the studied settings. The proposed prompt ablation is our inference, not a reproduction of those methods.

alternatives: Increase the step budget alone: does not isolate a targeted evidence rubric from a generic second look.
Change the retriever or use fixed evidence: a comparator already exists; its answer-support review is still missing.
Retrain a Self-RAG-style reflection policy: needs a new data/training study and is premature before this diagnostic.
proposed_change: Only the review instruction at a reconstructed first-submission state: generic second look versus explicit claim-to-evidence audit.
hypothesis: With the same model, evidence history, tools, and two-action continuation allowance, a targeted evidence audit may yield at least one additional substantive supported answer without breaking the two control cases.
expected_signal: Candidate repairs at least one more of the four answerable cases than the generic review, retains the previously supported answer and correct refusal, and adds no execution-error episode. Record whether repairs use already visible text or newly inspected evidence.
applicability: The saved failures include incorrect span selection after relevant text was seen and stopping before detailed evidence was inspected. A controlled continuation tests sensitivity to review instructions without weight changes.
differences: Five cases were chosen after outcomes were seen; this is a qualitative development diagnostic, not an efficacy estimate.
This is a prompt ablation with tools, not trained Self-RAG or ALCE benchmark reproduction.
Continuation from reconstructed saved state differs from a fresh full episode; improvements would not establish an end-to-end product gain.

stop_conditions: Do not start without separate execution approval and a priced, enforceable resource plan.
Stop before exceeding any aggregate request/token/context/time ceiling; count failed requests too; disable retries.
Use identical limits for both arms; any truncated/missing case remains missing, not a successful completion.
Stop on sandbox failure or evidence/corpus hash mismatch.

procedure: Validate the five source states, corpus, adapter identity and prompt hashes; independently check the answerability/control labels before running.

Build identical per-case contexts through the saved first draft submission. Keep reference answers, grader notes, post-hoc labels and this brief outside model input. Do not execute saved code on the host.

After separate approval, use one shared pinned model/runtime/tokenizer and Docker sandbox. Run each arm once per case in alternating order, with at most two additional actions and the aggregate ceilings above; reserve completion tokens within 8192 context.

Save every action/observation, attempted and accepted submissions, requests/tokens, timing and failures. Record whether supporting text was already visible or first obtained during continuation; this classification is an analysis annotation.

Have an identity-blind human inspect each material claim against its exact cited text, plus answer relevance and refusal correctness. Preserve model judgments separately. A valid quotation alone is not a pass.

Use the frozen thresholds only if the user first approves this exact draft. At least one extra supported substantive answer and no control/error regression justifies a larger separately approved study; otherwise stop and report null/harm. No outcome here establishes training improvement.
